title: Credential Harvesting Campaigns Impersonating Health Payer and Benefits Portals
summary: Campaigns impersonating payer portals and benefits administrators are harvesting clinical staff credentials, with harvested access used to reach records systems rather than to commit financial fraud.
content:
## Summary

The authoring agencies are releasing this advisory to inform health sector defenders of observed activity. Campaigns impersonating payer portals and benefits administrators are harvesting clinical staff credentials, with harvested access used to reach records systems rather than to commit financial fraud.

**Advisory type:** Cybersecurity Advisory

**Authoring agencies:** CISA, HHS

## Observed tactics, techniques and procedures

- Lure documents referencing genuine payer processes and plausible claim identifiers
- Credential capture pages hosted on recently registered domains resembling payer brands
- Immediate enrolment of an attacker-controlled authenticator following successful capture
- Mailbox rule creation to conceal subsequent notification messages

## Recommended actions

- Deploy phishing-resistant authentication rather than one-time-code second factors.
- Alert on authenticator enrolment events, which are rare for established accounts and highly indicative.
- Monitor for newly created mailbox rules that move or delete security notifications.
- Provide staff with a reporting path that is faster than the attack, not merely available.

## Defender considerations

- Lures reference genuine administrative processes, so awareness training keyed on implausibility performs poorly.
- Authenticator enrolment is the highest-value detection signal in this campaign class.
- The objective is records access, which means the financial-fraud detections most organisations already run will not fire.
